newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lira ERM entry political issue - Luxembourg minister.
newsitem.headline: Lira ERM entry political issue - Luxembourg minister.

text.p: The return of the Italian lira to the Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism is a political problem and stretches further than just the issue of the rate of entry, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Sunday.

"I don't mind discussing a lira more or a lira less but this is a political debate. I don't think the monetary committee was the appropriate body," Juncker, who is also finance minister, told reporters as he entered a meeting on Brussels on the issue.
"The problem is whether or not we want to put Italy in a position where it fulfils one of the Maastricht criteria," he added.
Membership of the ERM, a currency stability system, is seen as a prerequisite for joining a joint European currency in 1999, which is Italy's top goal.
Juncker and other EU ministers and central bank heads were holding talks on the issue in Brussels on Sunday, after the EU monetary committee failed to agree on the terms of lira entry on Saturday.
Italy asked for a rate of 1,010 lira to the German mark but its partners want a rate below 1,000 lira and some European ministers said the exchange rate was still the central issue at the talks.
"(The rate) is the most central issue," Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto told reporters.
